title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 41
paragraphs: Not much time had passed when the wife who had come in afterwards bore the Cleomenes we spoke of; and just as she was bringing to the light an heir to the Spartan kingdom, the former wife, who had been childless up to that point, by some chance conceived, happening to do so at just that moment. She was in truth with child, but the kinsfolk of the wife who had come in afterwards, when they heard about it, cried out against her, saying that she was making an empty boast and meant to pass off another's child as her own. Since they made a great show of indignation, and as the time drew near, the Ephors, being skeptical, sat around and watched the woman during the birth of her child; and she bore Dorieus, and then immediately conceived Leonidas and after him Cleombrotus—indeed, some even say that Cleombrotus and Leonidas were twins. The wife, however, who had borne Cleomenes and had come in after the first, daughter of Prinetades the son of Demarmenus, bore no more children.
